text:
"before u can be a great ______, u gotta be a great man first."

u can fill in the blank with whatever ur aspiring to be

not only is this true, it may help u avoid an identity crisis.

because if u are too tied up in ur occupation or title or w/e, u will learn -- as every man does -- that all this shit is temporary.

Fortune is a fickle mistress, we inhabit a kingdom primarily ruled by chance and error

and so when u stumble, the world will leave you grasping, wondering...wait, who the f am I?

if u are already thinking of yourself in terms of skills, traits, and attributes, this is not only more accurate as a self-image, but it makes u more flexible and versatile in the midst of shifting circumstances.

are you good with people, good with numbers, a good writer, reader, speaker, communicator...ur good at something, people keep u around for a reason.

u just have to re-align ur persona to these traits, rather not to some broad archetype like "I'm a lawyer." because that's not a thing.

this allows you to say "I'll figure it out" without LARPing. u know who u are as a human, u know exactly what u bring to the table, and no storm can take those traits from u.

now, during this process, u will realize that all ur mistakes were driven by "not being a great man."

u thought it was a fluke or a glitch

u thought wrong

it had nothing to do with bad luck, and it had nothing to do with your title or your career

it was 100% on you, the same way it always is

your vices simply got the best of you.

you were impatient, undisciplined, u lacked self-control, u were too emotional, and u let all these dogshit habits compound over years

all these vices were destined to sink you.

it didnt matter which path u went down. 

there was no way you would be great, even as a ditchdigger

why?

u already know why

because there is no path to being great at anything... that doesn't begin with you being a great man first.
